+# Restricted-owner held-file read observation
+
+This local functional observation closes the demonstrated FIFO-substitution
+hang in `operator_task_policy::open_held`. It does not close any of the eight
+release gates in the [development plan](../../docs/development/TRNM_AI_NATIVE_BLOCKCHAIN_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md).
+
+The ordinary restricted-owner startup reaches this reader through
+`Node::open_with_operator_task_policy` and `Journal::open`, for the retained
+owner lock and JSON records. A same-UID writer with access to the private journal
+can replace a checked regular file with a FIFO before its read-only open. The
+old open blocks before descriptor validation. This is a local availability
+boundary, not a demonstrated remote authorization or signature bypass.
+
+The fix adds `O_NONBLOCK` and keeps the existing descriptor identity checks and
+lock lifecycle. A private post-path-check helper provides the deterministic
+substitution seam. The retained test covers normal reads, wrong UID and
+FIFO/directory/symlink/hardlink replacements. The parent requires a completion
+marker, so a child test filter that executes no test cannot pass silently.
+Regular filesystem I/O is still not preemptible and receives no hard deadline
+claim from this flag.
+
+## Failed observations preserved
+
+- `owner-held-before.txt.gz`: an extracted-function syscall regression using the
+  old open flags failed after the bounded child remained blocked for five seconds.
+- `owner-held-after.txt.gz`: the corresponding initial extracted-function fix
+  passed. These are preliminary component runs, not complete crate tests.
+- `owner-held-clippy-initial.txt.gz`: actual crate checking rejected the initial
+  test's unsafe FIFO helper under `forbid(unsafe_code)`. The retained test now
+  uses safe `rustix::fs::mkfifoat`; no lint was weakened.
+- `scanner-before.txt.gz`: the separate PQ source inventory regression reproduced
+  acceptance of a same-size symlink substitution. `scanner-after.txt.gz` preserves
+  all 15 passing scanner controls. That fix was published separately as
+  `b58e36c5aa74343a0fe05e5b37f988c875c26acb`. The scanner still reports HOLD.
+
+## Final native checks
+
+The exact Rust inputs are listed in `owner-held-final-source.sha256`.
+The locked, offline build used the repository's package optimization settings,
+with `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and one Cargo build job
+to avoid deleting other work from a low-disk environment. This is a functional
+regression build, not the original resource or test-profile performance gate.
+
+- `owner-held-native.txt.gz`: actual `trnm-pon-node` library regression passed.
+- `owner-held-policy-tests.txt.gz`: all 18 selected owner-policy tests passed;

+  The other 1,130 library tests were not selected and are not claimed passed.

+  inventory, 16 project-boundary controls and 43 source-integrity controls passed.

+# Native apply cache experiment: rejected default integration
+
+The fixed first campaign rejects enabling this optimization. All eight cells preserve full roots, stored rows, actual SQL counts, callback counts and rollback. Six timing cells pass, but two cold sparse cells fail the criterion fixed before execution. The default implementation is restored; the rejected candidate remains only under `cfg(test)` for reproducibility. No Host, confirmation, security or product gate is closed.
+
+## Source and execution
+
+The measured candidate is local commit `d685a14ac2b2ce0a30e7bacee6eb29290d8248cf`, tree `88ddb8b5d9c3a4885ed00a69804700c02cf44a65`, based on `f9977c5d6d1b57880967ef36dcd1570010cbbe4f`. Its complete patch is retained in the raw archive. Original Rust 1.95.0 profiles and locked packages were used, with one build job. The test-only rusqlite trace feature adds no package and is absent from normal production dependencies.
+
+The measured source passed eight new native differential/adversarial tests in both test and release profiles, plus three existing real publication/cancellation/reopen tests in the test profile. The first attempted test observer failed the project's unsafe-code prohibition; its full compiler error is retained. The observer was corrected to the dependency's safe trace API, without weakening that prohibition. The first CI-contract check exposed stale inline source hashes; the exact hashes were corrected without changing the gates.
+
+Final isolation source `1a7357936942e0e8a3564026e5257dc95cba6ea4` restores `native_authenticated.rs` and the existing batch test file byte-for-byte to the base. `native_store.rs` differs only by its test-module declaration. An independent code review found the relocated candidate algorithm unchanged apart from module qualification, visibility, comments and formatting. It is not a production fallback.
+
+## Fixed complete-apply campaign
+
+There are 512/1,024 accounts, one or one-quarter changed accounts, and cold or parent-graph-warmed arithmetic caches: eight cells, twelve alternating pairs each, three arms per pair. All 288 samples, 96 pair records, eight cell records and the final false qualification summary are retained. The original function, candidate and uncached fallback execute in one release test binary.
+
+Each timed interval includes complete apply through returned-root disposal. Transaction begin/rollback, parent-cache warming, cache setup/destruction and post-call inspection are outside that interval. The SQL database is in memory; SQLite page/statement caches are not declared cold. Actual SQL counters come from a separate identical-input equivalence replay, not the primary timing interval. These observations cannot establish complete publish, disk, network, scheduling, hostile-W1 or confirmation cost.
+
+The preregistered component criterion requires at least 5% median improvement and no more than 10% p95 regression in every cell, alongside complete equivalence. With twelve values, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. The failed cells are:
+

+- 1,024 accounts, one change, cold cache: median ratio **0.976192**, only 2.38% improvement, below the required 5%; p95 ratio **0.649718**.

+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
+struct SqlObservation {
+    selects: u64,
+    writes: u64,
+    statements: u64,
+    // Actual bound statements are retained in correctness tests only. Timing
+    // observations use counters without expansion/allocation on each read.
+    sequence: Vec<String>,
+}
+
+struct TraceState {
+    observation: RefCell<SqlObservation>,
+    capture: bool,
+    failed: std::cell::Cell<bool>,
+}
+thread_local! {
+    // Test workers are independent threads. Rc also makes a guard !Send, so
+    // its callback state and cleanup cannot migrate to another test worker.
+    static ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE: RefCell<Option<std::rc::Rc<TraceState>>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
+}
+
+struct SqlTrace<'db> {
+    db: &'db Connection,
+    state: std::rc::Rc<TraceState>,
+}
+impl<'db> SqlTrace<'db> {
+    fn new(db: &'db Connection, capture: bool) -> Self {
+        let state = std::rc::Rc::new(TraceState {
+            observation: RefCell::default(),
+            capture,
+            failed: std::cell::Cell::new(false),
+        });
+        ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| {
+            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
+            assert!(slot.is_none(), "only one traced test connection per worker");
+            *slot = Some(std::rc::Rc::clone(&state));
+        });
+        // These test-owned connections never have a TransactionScope observer
+        // or Node owner. The dependency's safe wrapper owns the SQLite ABI.
+        let guard = Self { db, state };
+        db.trace_v2(
+            rusqlite::trace::TraceEventCodes::SQLITE_TRACE_STMT,
+            Some(sql_trace),
+        );
+        guard
+    }
+    fn observation(&self) -> SqlObservation {
+        assert!(!self.state.failed.get(), "SQL trace must be complete");
+        self.state.observation.borrow().clone()
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for SqlTrace<'_> {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        self.db
+            .trace_v2(rusqlite::trace::TraceEventCodes::empty(), None);
+        ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| {
+            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
+            if slot
+                .as_ref()
+                .is_some_and(|state| std::rc::Rc::ptr_eq(state, &self.state))
+            {
+                slot.take();
+            } else {
+                self.state.failed.set(true);
+            }
+        });
+    }
+}
+fn sql_trace(event: rusqlite::trace::TraceEvent<'_>) {
+    let rusqlite::trace::TraceEvent::Stmt(statement, _) = event else {
+        return;
+    };
+    let state = ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| slot.borrow().clone());
+    let Some(state) = state else {
+        return;
+    };
+    // The wrapper catches ABI unwinds. Mark our observation failed as well so
+    // a swallowed diagnostic failure can never look like complete evidence.
+    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
+        let sql = statement.sql();
+        let verb = sql.split_ascii_whitespace().next();
+        let mut observation = state.observation.borrow_mut();
+        observation.statements += 1;
+        // Count actual executed statements, not prepares or expected graph
+        // visits. This test corpus contains only these fixed SQL verbs. Unknown
+        // statements fail the observation rather than being guessed readonly.
+        // Trigger events use the original statement's SQL, not synthetic text.
+        match verb {
+            Some("SELECT") => observation.selects += 1,
+            Some("INSERT" | "UPDATE" | "DELETE" | "ALTER" | "CREATE" | "DROP") => {
+                observation.writes += 1
+            }
+            _ => state.failed.set(true),
+        }
+        if state.capture {
+            match statement.expanded_sql() {
+                Some(value) => observation.sequence.push(value),
+                None => state.failed.set(true),
+            }
+        }
+    }));
+    if result.is_err() {
+        state.failed.set(true);
+    }
+}

+fn observed(
+    arm: Arm,
+    db: &Connection,
+    root: &Root,
+    deltas: &[crate::store::Delta],
+    cache: &LiftCache,
+    mut checkpoint: impl FnMut(usize) -> Result<()>,
+) -> (Verdict, usize, SqlObservation, Stored) {
+    let mut calls = 0;
+    let trace = SqlTrace::new(db, true);
+    let result = verdict(run(
+        arm,
+        db,
+        root,
+        deltas,
+        &mut || {
+            calls += 1;
+            checkpoint(calls)
+        },
+        cache,
+    ));
+    let sql = trace.observation();
+    drop(trace);
+    (result, calls, sql, stored(db))
+}

+fn sample(
+    arm: Arm,
+    db: &Connection,
+    state: &State,
+    root: &Root,
+    changes: &[crate::store::Delta],
+    warm: bool,
+) -> Sample {
+    // Every sample starts with a fresh arithmetic cache. "Warm" means exactly
+    // the complete parent graph was checked once, as in publish_with_readback;
+    // it does not mean a previous successful successor/rollback warmed it.
+    let cache = LiftCache::default();
+    if warm {
+        verify_with_lifts(db, root, state, &mut || Ok(()), Some(&cache)).unwrap();
+    }
+    let decode_before = cache.decode_observation();
+    let transaction = db.unchecked_transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut progress = 0;
+    let before_cpu = thread_cpu_ns();
+    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
+    let returned = verdict(run(
+        arm,
+        &transaction,
+        root,
+        changes,
+        &mut || {
+            progress += 1;
+            Ok(())
+        },
+        &cache,
+    ));
+    std::hint::black_box(&returned);
+    // Preserve the complete returned value for equality, then dispose of the
+    // call's return before ending its interval. The same small copy is charged
+    // in all arms. SQL transaction setup/rollback and inspection are outside.

+//! Descriptor substitution tests for the actual restricted-owner journal reader.
+use super::*;
+use std::os::unix::fs::{symlink, PermissionsExt};
+use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+
+fn fifo(path: &Path) {
+    rustix::fs::mkfifoat(
+        rustix::fs::CWD,
+        path,
+        rustix::fs::Mode::RUSR | rustix::fs::Mode::WUSR,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+}

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "run only by the bounded subprocess regression"]
+fn held_file_substitution_child() {
+    let work = std::env::current_dir().unwrap();
+    for kind in ["regular", "fifo", "directory", "symlink", "hardlink"] {
+        let path = work.join(format!("journal-{kind}"));
+        fs::write(&path, b"retained journal bytes").unwrap();
+        fs::set_permissions(&path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600)).unwrap();
+        let before = fs::symlink_metadata(&path).unwrap();
+        // Use the precise production seam after the checked pathname metadata,
+        // without relying on scheduler timing to win a rename/open race.
+        if kind != "regular" {
+            let retained = work.join(format!("retained-{kind}"));
+            fs::rename(&path, &retained).unwrap();
+            match kind {
+                "fifo" => fifo(&path),
+                "directory" => fs::create_dir(&path).unwrap(),
+                "symlink" => symlink(&retained, &path).unwrap(),
+                "hardlink" => fs::hard_link(&retained, &path).unwrap(),
+                _ => unreachable!(),
+            }
+        }
+        let result = open_held_after_check(&path, &before);
+        if kind == "regular" {
+            let mut file = result.unwrap();
+            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
+            file.read_to_end(&mut bytes).unwrap();
+            assert_eq!(bytes, b"retained journal bytes");
+            // Also retain the complete entrypoint, including the UID check.
+            assert!(open_held(&path, before.uid()).is_ok());
+            assert!(matches!(
+                open_held(&path, before.uid().wrapping_add(1)),
+                Err(PolicyError::Journal)
+            ));
+        } else {
+            assert!(matches!(result, Err(PolicyError::Journal)), "{kind}");
+        }
+    }
+    fs::write(work.join("completed"), b"all substitution cases executed").unwrap();
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn held_file_substitutions_reject_without_blocking() {
+    let work = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let mut child = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
+        .args(["--ignored", "--nocapture", "held_file_substitution_child"])
+        .current_dir(work.path())
+        .stdin(Stdio::null())
+        .spawn()
+        .unwrap();
+    let started = Instant::now();
+    loop {
+        if let Some(status) = child.try_wait().unwrap() {
+            assert!(status.success(), "substitution child failed: {status}");
+            assert_eq!(
+                fs::read(work.path().join("completed")).unwrap(),
+                b"all substitution cases executed"
+            );
+            break;
+        }
+        if started.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(5) {
+            child.kill().unwrap();
+            child.wait().unwrap();
+            panic!("journal descriptor open blocked on a substituted special file");
+        }

+}"}]}

+# Restricted-owner held-file read observation
+
+This local functional observation closes the demonstrated FIFO-substitution
+hang in `operator_task_policy::open_held`. It does not close any of the eight
+release gates in the [development plan](../../docs/development/TRNM_AI_NATIVE_BLOCKCHAIN_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md).
+
+The ordinary restricted-owner startup reaches this reader through
+`Node::open_with_operator_task_policy` and `Journal::open`, for the retained
+owner lock and JSON records. A same-UID writer with access to the private journal
+can replace a checked regular file with a FIFO before its read-only open. The
+old open blocks before descriptor validation. This is a local availability
+boundary, not a demonstrated remote authorization or signature bypass.
+
+The fix adds `O_NONBLOCK` and keeps the existing descriptor identity checks and
+lock lifecycle. A private post-path-check helper provides the deterministic
+substitution seam. The retained test covers normal reads, wrong UID and
+FIFO/directory/symlink/hardlink replacements. The parent requires a completion
+marker, so a child test filter that executes no test cannot pass silently.
+Regular filesystem I/O is still not preemptible and receives no hard deadline
+claim from this flag.
+
+## Failed observations preserved
+
+- `owner-held-before.txt.gz`: an extracted-function syscall regression using the
+  old open flags failed after the bounded child remained blocked for five seconds.
+- `owner-held-after.txt.gz`: the corresponding initial extracted-function fix
+  passed. These are preliminary component runs, not complete crate tests.
+- `owner-held-clippy-initial.txt.gz`: actual crate checking rejected the initial
+  test's unsafe FIFO helper under `forbid(unsafe_code)`. The retained test now
+  uses safe `rustix::fs::mkfifoat`; no lint was weakened.
+- `scanner-before.txt.gz`: the separate PQ source inventory regression reproduced
+  acceptance of a same-size symlink substitution. `scanner-after.txt.gz` preserves
+  all 15 passing scanner controls. That fix was published separately as
+  `b58e36c5aa74343a0fe05e5b37f988c875c26acb`. The scanner still reports HOLD.
+
+## Final native checks
+
+The exact Rust inputs are listed in `owner-held-final-source.sha256`.
+The locked, offline build used the repository's package optimization settings,
+with `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and one Cargo build job
+to avoid deleting other work from a low-disk environment. This is a functional
+regression build, not the original resource or test-profile performance gate.
+
+- `owner-held-native.txt.gz`: actual `trnm-pon-node` library regression passed.
+- `owner-held-policy-tests.txt.gz`: all 18 selected owner-policy tests passed;

+  The other 1,130 library tests were not selected and are not claimed passed.

+  inventory, 16 project-boundary controls and 43 source-integrity controls passed.

+# Native apply cache experiment: rejected default integration
+
+The fixed first campaign rejects enabling this optimization. All eight cells preserve full roots, stored rows, actual SQL counts, callback counts and rollback. Six timing cells pass, but two cold sparse cells fail the criterion fixed before execution. The default implementation is restored; the rejected candidate remains only under `cfg(test)` for reproducibility. No Host, confirmation, security or product gate is closed.
+
+## Source and execution
+
+The measured candidate is local commit `d685a14ac2b2ce0a30e7bacee6eb29290d8248cf`, tree `88ddb8b5d9c3a4885ed00a69804700c02cf44a65`, based on `f9977c5d6d1b57880967ef36dcd1570010cbbe4f`. Its complete patch is retained in the raw archive. Original Rust 1.95.0 profiles and locked packages were used, with one build job. The test-only rusqlite trace feature adds no package and is absent from normal production dependencies.
+
+The measured source passed eight new native differential/adversarial tests in both test and release profiles, plus three existing real publication/cancellation/reopen tests in the test profile. The first attempted test observer failed the project's unsafe-code prohibition; its full compiler error is retained. The observer was corrected to the dependency's safe trace API, without weakening that prohibition. The first CI-contract check exposed stale inline source hashes; the exact hashes were corrected without changing the gates.
+
+Final isolation source `1a7357936942e0e8a3564026e5257dc95cba6ea4` restores `native_authenticated.rs` and the existing batch test file byte-for-byte to the base. `native_store.rs` differs only by its test-module declaration. An independent code review found the relocated candidate algorithm unchanged apart from module qualification, visibility, comments and formatting. It is not a production fallback.
+
+## Fixed complete-apply campaign
+
+There are 512/1,024 accounts, one or one-quarter changed accounts, and cold or parent-graph-warmed arithmetic caches: eight cells, twelve alternating pairs each, three arms per pair. All 288 samples, 96 pair records, eight cell records and the final false qualification summary are retained. The original function, candidate and uncached fallback execute in one release test binary.
+
+Each timed interval includes complete apply through returned-root disposal. Transaction begin/rollback, parent-cache warming, cache setup/destruction and post-call inspection are outside that interval. The SQL database is in memory; SQLite page/statement caches are not declared cold. Actual SQL counters come from a separate identical-input equivalence replay, not the primary timing interval. These observations cannot establish complete publish, disk, network, scheduling, hostile-W1 or confirmation cost.
+
+The preregistered component criterion requires at least 5% median improvement and no more than 10% p95 regression in every cell, alongside complete equivalence. With twelve values, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. The failed cells are:
+

+- 1,024 accounts, one change, cold cache: median ratio **0.976192**, only 2.38% improvement, below the required 5%; p95 ratio **0.649718**.

+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
+struct SqlObservation {
+    selects: u64,
+    writes: u64,
+    statements: u64,
+    // Actual bound statements are retained in correctness tests only. Timing
+    // observations use counters without expansion/allocation on each read.
+    sequence: Vec<String>,
+}
+
+struct TraceState {
+    observation: RefCell<SqlObservation>,
+    capture: bool,
+    failed: std::cell::Cell<bool>,
+}
+thread_local! {
+    // Test workers are independent threads. Rc also makes a guard !Send, so
+    // its callback state and cleanup cannot migrate to another test worker.
+    static ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE: RefCell<Option<std::rc::Rc<TraceState>>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
+}
+
+struct SqlTrace<'db> {
+    db: &'db Connection,
+    state: std::rc::Rc<TraceState>,
+}
+impl<'db> SqlTrace<'db> {
+    fn new(db: &'db Connection, capture: bool) -> Self {
+        let state = std::rc::Rc::new(TraceState {
+            observation: RefCell::default(),
+            capture,
+            failed: std::cell::Cell::new(false),
+        });
+        ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| {
+            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
+            assert!(slot.is_none(), "only one traced test connection per worker");
+            *slot = Some(std::rc::Rc::clone(&state));
+        });
+        // These test-owned connections never have a TransactionScope observer
+        // or Node owner. The dependency's safe wrapper owns the SQLite ABI.
+        let guard = Self { db, state };
+        db.trace_v2(
+            rusqlite::trace::TraceEventCodes::SQLITE_TRACE_STMT,
+            Some(sql_trace),
+        );
+        guard
+    }
+    fn observation(&self) -> SqlObservation {
+        assert!(!self.state.failed.get(), "SQL trace must be complete");
+        self.state.observation.borrow().clone()
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for SqlTrace<'_> {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        self.db
+            .trace_v2(rusqlite::trace::TraceEventCodes::empty(), None);
+        ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| {
+            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
+            if slot
+                .as_ref()
+                .is_some_and(|state| std::rc::Rc::ptr_eq(state, &self.state))
+            {
+                slot.take();
+            } else {
+                self.state.failed.set(true);
+            }
+        });
+    }
+}
+fn sql_trace(event: rusqlite::trace::TraceEvent<'_>) {
+    let rusqlite::trace::TraceEvent::Stmt(statement, _) = event else {
+        return;
+    };
+    let state = ACTIVE_SQL_TRACE.with(|slot| slot.borrow().clone());
+    let Some(state) = state else {
+        return;
+    };
+    // The wrapper catches ABI unwinds. Mark our observation failed as well so
+    // a swallowed diagnostic failure can never look like complete evidence.
+    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
+        let sql = statement.sql();
+        let verb = sql.split_ascii_whitespace().next();
+        let mut observation = state.observation.borrow_mut();
+        observation.statements += 1;
+        // Count actual executed statements, not prepares or expected graph
+        // visits. This test corpus contains only these fixed SQL verbs. Unknown
+        // statements fail the observation rather than being guessed readonly.
+        // Trigger events use the original statement's SQL, not synthetic text.
+        match verb {
+            Some("SELECT") => observation.selects += 1,
+            Some("INSERT" | "UPDATE" | "DELETE" | "ALTER" | "CREATE" | "DROP") => {
+                observation.writes += 1
+            }
+            _ => state.failed.set(true),
+        }
+        if state.capture {
+            match statement.expanded_sql() {
+                Some(value) => observation.sequence.push(value),
+                None => state.failed.set(true),
+            }
+        }
+    }));
+    if result.is_err() {
+        state.failed.set(true);
+    }
+}

+fn observed(
+    arm: Arm,
+    db: &Connection,
+    root: &Root,
+    deltas: &[crate::store::Delta],
+    cache: &LiftCache,
+    mut checkpoint: impl FnMut(usize) -> Result<()>,
+) -> (Verdict, usize, SqlObservation, Stored) {
+    let mut calls = 0;
+    let trace = SqlTrace::new(db, true);
+    let result = verdict(run(
+        arm,
+        db,
+        root,
+        deltas,
+        &mut || {
+            calls += 1;
+            checkpoint(calls)
+        },
+        cache,
+    ));
+    let sql = trace.observation();
+    drop(trace);
+    (result, calls, sql, stored(db))
+}

+fn sample(
+    arm: Arm,
+    db: &Connection,
+    state: &State,
+    root: &Root,
+    changes: &[crate::store::Delta],
+    warm: bool,
+) -> Sample {
+    // Every sample starts with a fresh arithmetic cache. "Warm" means exactly
+    // the complete parent graph was checked once, as in publish_with_readback;
+    // it does not mean a previous successful successor/rollback warmed it.
+    let cache = LiftCache::default();
+    if warm {
+        verify_with_lifts(db, root, state, &mut || Ok(()), Some(&cache)).unwrap();
+    }
+    let decode_before = cache.decode_observation();
+    let transaction = db.unchecked_transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut progress = 0;
+    let before_cpu = thread_cpu_ns();
+    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
+    let returned = verdict(run(
+        arm,
+        &transaction,
+        root,
+        changes,
+        &mut || {
+            progress += 1;
+            Ok(())
+        },
+        &cache,
+    ));
+    std::hint::black_box(&returned);
+    // Preserve the complete returned value for equality, then dispose of the
+    // call's return before ending its interval. The same small copy is charged
+    // in all arms. SQL transaction setup/rollback and inspection are outside.
+    let result = returned.clone();
+    drop(returned);

+    let cpu_ns = before_cpu

+    let diagnostic_cache = LiftCache::default();

+    let mut diagnostic_progress = 0;

+        root,

+        && stored(&transaction) == rows;

+        progress,

+//! Descriptor substitution tests for the actual restricted-owner journal reader.
+use super::*;
+use std::os::unix::fs::{symlink, PermissionsExt};
+use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+
+fn fifo(path: &Path) {
+    rustix::fs::mkfifoat(
+        rustix::fs::CWD,
+        path,
+        rustix::fs::Mode::RUSR | rustix::fs::Mode::WUSR,
+    )
+    .unwrap();

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "run only by the bounded subprocess regression"]
+fn held_file_substitution_child() {
+    let work = std::env::current_dir().unwrap();
+    for kind in ["regular", "fifo", "directory", "symlink", "hardlink"] {
+        let path = work.join(format!("journal-{kind}"));
+        fs::write(&path, b"retained journal bytes").unwrap();
+        fs::set_permissions(&path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600)).unwrap();
+        let before = fs::symlink_metadata(&path).unwrap();
+        // Use the precise production seam after the checked pathname metadata,
+        // without relying on scheduler timing to win a rename/open race.
+        if kind != "regular" {
+            let retained = work.join(format!("retained-{kind}"));
+            fs::rename(&path, &retained).unwrap();
+            match kind {
+                "fifo" => fifo(&path),
+                "directory" => fs::create_dir(&path).unwrap(),
+                "symlink" => symlink(&retained, &path).unwrap(),
+                "hardlink" => fs::hard_link(&retained, &path).unwrap(),
+                _ => unreachable!(),
+            }
+        }
+        let result = open_held_after_check(&path, &before);
+        if kind == "regular" {
+            let mut file = result.unwrap();
+            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
+            file.read_to_end(&mut bytes).unwrap();
+            assert_eq!(bytes, b"retained journal bytes");
+            // Also retain the complete entrypoint, including the UID check.
+            assert!(open_held(&path, before.uid()).is_ok());
+            assert!(matches!(
+                open_held(&path, before.uid().wrapping_add(1)),
+                Err(PolicyError::Journal)
+            ));
+        } else {
+            assert!(matches!(result, Err(PolicyError::Journal)), "{kind}");
+        }
+    }
+    fs::write(work.join("completed"), b"all substitution cases executed").unwrap();
+}
